goal: Take apart what an image reference really means — registry, repository, tag, digest and OCI manifest — see how the kubelet hands it to a CRI runtime, and prove why a moved tag breaks reproducibility while a digest cannot.
produces: An image-catalog Pod serving data/image-inventory.csv and data/reference-forms.tsv, with its resolved status.imageID captured
A digest-pinned Pod repaired from a stale sha256 reference to the digest this cluster actually resolved
An imagePullPolicy matrix showing Always, IfNotPresent and an ErrImageNeverPull for a Never-policy image
concepts: Image reference anatomy and the implicit docker.io/library/ + :latest defaults
OCI image spec: index -> manifest -> config + content-addressed layers
spec.image is what you asked for; status.imageID is what the runtime resolved
imagePullPolicy semantics and defaults; CRI is the kubelet-to-containerd boundary
